assessment: Preassembly plausibly lets workers check the selected configuration before dispatch while retaining removable partitions. Repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes, so this workflow sometimes approaches the time target; its 11-minute overall median and customer difficulties do not establish success. Mixed batches contain every extreme delay, but layout complexity could explain that association. A concrete limit on a width-only insertion explanation is D2-O5: widths overlap between first-attempt and retried parts. This weakens width alone as a sufficient discriminator without excluding fit problems. Missing-part reports are not independently verified physical omissions in all five cases. All causal accounts below remain hypotheses within this synthetic case.

openings.claim: Switching configurations may increase selection and checking time even when the parts and insertion method remain unchanged.
openings.delta: Separates a configuration-switch cost from intrinsic layout complexity and insertion difficulty.
openings.prediction: For matched layouts and workers, interleaved orders take longer specifically during selection or checking than repeated-layout blocks; a complexity-only account predicts no comparable switching difference.
openings.probe: Use 12 spare-board samples as six matched pairs across the three layouts and two workers. Counterbalance block/interleaved sequence and record selection, insertion, checking and packing separately; independently count required components. Treat the small comparison as directional evidence.
assumptions: The comparison fits available working time without delaying the fixed delivery date.

openings.claim: The generic three-layout diagram may leave the role of a present, correct short partition ambiguous.
openings.delta: Tests instruction ambiguity separately from physical component omission.
openings.prediction: With contents independently verified, an ordered-layout diagram reduces short-partition questions and unaided arrangement failures relative to the current diagram.
openings.probe: Assign the ten participants to matched five-person groups using verified sample organizers and either diagram. Record correct placement, assistance requests and completion time. Measure preparation time and replacement-diagram cost before adoption.
assumptions: Instructions replace the existing diagram within both cost caps.
Parts, footprint, capacity, removability, accepted counts and colors remain unchanged.
Five participants per condition provide exploratory evidence, not pilot success certification.
